paper.title_en: A New Gravitational Wave Power Law from Dissipative Sound Waves in Cosmological Phase Transitions
paper.abstract_en: Power-law behavior in cosmological gravitational wave (GW) spectra reveals the physical nature of their sources. For sound waves generated by cosmological first-order phase transitions, we identify a new high-frequency power law arising from the dissipative evolution of the acoustic source. In a dissipative plasma, the GW spectrum acquires an additional $q^{-2}$ suppression relative to the perfect-fluid result in the late-time, strong-damping limit. The exponent is largely insensitive to the source profile, while the turnover and suppression strength probe plasma transport and the source lifetime. In particular, the turnover frequency in weakly coupled hidden sector plasmas is sensitive to the underlying gauge coupling and can lie in the millihertz band targeted by space-based interferometers, opening a way to probe microscopic plasma dynamics through the detailed GW spectrum.
